dedupe_keys.name: bundesnetzagentur analytical cost model for the broadband network analytisches kostenmodell breitbandnetz

description: The Bundesnetzagentur's analytical cost model for the broadband network is a bottom-up engineering and economic model of an efficient fixed broadband network, which the German regulator uses to check the costs of regulated wholesale services. It was commissioned from WIK-Consult in 2004 and 2005 and builds the network element by element, covering the xDSL access and concentration segments and the transport network above them, so that the cost of each network element can be derived from dimensioning rules, equipment prices and cost of capital. The agency presented the reference document at an information event on 9 March 2005 and received twelve written comments by 30 April 2005; later versions (the page path names a second generation, Breitbandnetz 2.x) followed as networks moved to next-generation access. Coverage: Germany. Format and access: reference documents and consultation papers published as PDFs on the Bundesnetzagentur site, in German, free to read; the model software itself is not published. Caveats: a regulatory costing model whose parameters reflect German market decisions of their time; the network it models is a hypothetical efficient operator, not Deutsche Telekom's actual plant. Simulation uses: cost-based economic appraisal of fixed network investment and wholesale pricing, and a reference for element-level dimensioning of access and transport networks. Related records: the Bundesnetzagentur mobile network cost model and the Arcep mobile cost model are companion regulatory models, and pysim5g gives an open techno-economic model for mobile networks.
